name: FHL operations direct jobs, annual-average FTE (12-month basis)

UW EIR bases direct jobs on FTE; this is also the job concept of the OFM indirect/induced coefficients (annual-average jobs) and of QCEW (annual average of monthly jobs)

name: Washington induced output per $ of resident household (Type I labor) income
used_in: state induced scale s = WA_IND_K / OFM k
source: Parker Strategy Group (2024) UW Economic Impact Report FY23 (IMPLAN), pp. 6-11, https://cdn.uw.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/18/2024/10/29155253/PSG-UW-Economic-Impact-Report.pdf p. 9 (UW research enterprise table); WWU CEBR (Dec 2024) Washington State Ferry System Economic Impact Study, Tables 1, 4, 24, https://cbe.wwu.edu/sites/cbe.wwu.edu/files/2025-01/WWU%20Ferry%20Study%20Full%20Report.pdf Tables 1-2; OFM 2012 closure (this model)
basis: derived: central = UW research enterprise IMPLAN induced output 737,574,634 / Type I labor income (736,445,473 + 202,789,107) = 0.7853; low = WSF statewide IMPLAN induced labor income per $ of Type I labor income (1.38/1.11 - 1 = 0.2432) relative to the OFM closure (0.4790) = scale 0.5078, times OFM 1.5291; high (extreme bound only) = OFM household closure as built (1.5291), which treats all PCE as funded by labor income with no tax, saving or transfer-income leakage. Monte Carlo: triangular(low, central, 0.60 x OFM = 0.9175); 0.60 x OFM is an assumption allowing FHL households (pay about half of UW research staff pay per job) a higher consumption share of income than UW research households. The one-at-a-time sensitivity swings this input over its Monte Carlo support (low to 0.60 x OFM); the closure as built enters only as the named variant VARIANT_OFM_CLOSURE_AS_BUILT

name: San Juan County induced output per $ of resident household (Type I labor) income
used_in: county induced scale s = SJC_IND_K / closure k
source: WWU CEBR (Dec 2024) Washington State Ferry System Economic Impact Study, Tables 1, 4, 24, https://cbe.wwu.edu/sites/cbe.wwu.edu/files/2025-01/WWU%20Ferry%20Study%20Full%20Report.pdf Table 24 (Route 80, San Juan County); WWU CEBR San Juan County profile 2025, https://cbe.wwu.edu/sites/cbe.wwu.edu/files/2025-10/San%20Juan%20profile_2025_FINAL.pdf (people_and_local/san_juan_county_context.csv); FLQ closures (this model)
basis: derived: central = WSF Route 80 San Juan County IMPLAN induced output 9,797,191 / Type I labor income (24,703,872 + 1,217,462) = 0.3780, divided by the county resident share of workplace labor income 0.94 (about 6% of county jobs are held by in-commuters, WWU CEBR 2025) to express it per $ of resident income = 0.4021. Cross-check: the WA OFM-to-IMPLAN ratio applied to the county SLQ closure gives 0.751 x 0.514 = 0.386. Low (extreme bound) = FLQ-scaled household closure at delta 0.25 (0.1933); high (extreme bound) = SLQ-scaled household closure as built (0.7510). Monte Carlo: triangular(mc_low, central, mc_high) with mc_low = the same Route 80 benchmark matched on induced labor income instead of output (0.0875 / 0.94 per resident $, divided by the central closure's 0.2228 and times its k 0.7386 = 0.3086) and mc_high = central + (central - mc_low) (assumption: symmetric; a single county IMPLAN benchmark, and Route 80 crews may partly live off-island, which would depress it). The one-at-a-time sensitivity swings this input over its Monte Carlo support; the FLQ and SLQ closures enter only as the named variants VARIANT_SJC_FLQ_HOUSEHOLDS and VARIANT_OFM_CLOSURE_AS_BUILT

basis: measured/assumption: 88% of county workers live and work in the county; about 6% commute in (WWU CEBR 2025 job flows); low = 0.88, central = 1 - 0.06, high = no leakage. Seasonal non-resident accommodation/food workers (July-August 1,515-1,538 vs annual average 988) support the low

name: Jobs-per-$ update 2012->2024: weight on CPI-only deflation (0 = QCEW pay growth, 1 = CPI-U only), both regions
basis: assumption: e2024 = e2012 / (pay_ratio^(1-w) x CPI_ratio^w). Pay growth in low-wage sectors 2012-2024 (IO-50 1.84, IO-49 1.76, IO-52 2.28 vs CPI 1.37) partly reflects WA minimum-wage increases rather than output prices, so the pay-only update understates jobs per $; the CPI-only update ignores productivity growth and overstates them.
